content: Floor-plan images carry no metric scale; metres-per-pixel must be established from at least one known real-world reference before any metric claim is made. Established practice: Floorbase calibrates once per sheet immediately after import and then verifies against a second, independent known dimension (accept within 2 percent, otherwise recalibrate), warning that skewed scans disagree between axes; the indoor-mapping-wayfinding standard requires a known reference dimension and states that if none is recoverable the run 'should abort rather than emit pixel-space geometry' because 'an invented scale corrupts every weight in the routing graph'; CRITIR recommends registering 2-4 measurements and using the median, flagging outliers, because a single bad reference poisons everything downstream. Documented failure signatures: a door read as '1200 metres' when detection ran in pixels and scale was never applied; 'scale drift across floor levels' when each level was exported at a different resolution (mitigation: compare ppm across levels and enforce a global calibration against a constant such as a 1.5m standard corridor width); and image resizing invalidating a previously recorded scale (halving width doubles m/px and halves all reported distances if the old factor is reused). Print-relevant conversions: a 4m wall spanning 400px gives 0.01 m/px, and a 1000px segment is then 10m. The floor-plan-scale-calculator guidance also warns that a printed 1:100 ratio depends on the physical sheet size, and that 'viewing a PDF on a screen or printing with fit-to-page changes the relationship with a ruler measurement' - so a scale derived from a PDF viewer, not the raster, is wrong.
